newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS -Gilts boosted as rates kept on hold.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS -Gilts boosted as rates kept on hold.

text.p: Expectations for British gilts turned positive on Thursday, paving the way for short-term outperformance against core European bonds and a further steepening of the yield curve, analysts said.

Recent data suggesting the economy was weaker than had previously been thought, boosted the market. This view was confirmed by the decision to leave interest rates unchanged after the monthly meeting between Chancellor to the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Wednesday.
"This is the dawn of a new day in the gilt market," said Andrew Roberts senior bond strategist at UBS in London. "It is one of the few days when you can actually see a turnaround in expectations."
He said people had been waiting for confirmation that rates would not be raised.
"The economy is far weaker than people expect, it is going to undershoot expectations and we're going to have fewer rate rises and a much better market performance," said Roberts at UBS.
Katy Peters, economist at Daiwa Europe in London agreed that the short-term outlook for gilts was positive.
"We've had good RPI data, there was no move in rates, the spread has narrowed in sharply over Germany and the short sterling contract is up very sharply," she said.

December retail prices rose 0.3 percent in the month, compared with 0.1 percent in November, giving a year-on-year rise of 2.5 percent versus 2.7 percent previously. Both were lower than expectations. RPIX rose 3.1 percent, in line with forecasts and compared with 3.3 percent in November.
The 10-year gilt/Bund spread was at 182 basis points at 1407 GMT, compared with 191 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Short sterling was better bid, with the March contract trading at 93.60, up 16 basis points on the day. Further out, the June, September and December contracts were also trading higher.

"If short sterling was only up in March, that would be people saying "no rate hike this month, no big deal'. The fact that it is up for more than March suggests people are saying it's a soft landing process," said Andrew Roberts. "That's what we are pricing in."

But Huw Roberts, European bond strategist at NatWest Capital Markets in London, was more cautious. He said the short sterling strip was well bid in reaction to the unrealistic profile it had been discounting at the end of last year.
"This is a reaction rather than short sterling becoming overtly bullish," he said.
He said Thursday's move in the gilt market could be something of a short squeeze.

"Certainly from what we have seen, whilst the international account holders have been trying to buy gilts, the domestics have been a lot more cautious, and we go along with that," said NatWest's Roberts.
December retail sales data were due on January 22, fourth quarter GDP on January 27 and the next monetary meeting on Febraury 5.

"I wouldn't be surprised if we get firmish retail sales -- on the back of good Christmas shopping -- and pretty healthy growth in Q4 from the statistics at the end of last year. Then all of a sudden, the pressures will be back on for another rate hike," said Huw Roberts.

"I agree with the premise that gilts are going to offer very real value and could be one of the best performing bond markets in 1997, but on the question of when, I am conservative. Now is probably not the time," he said.
